facts.claim: pageHtml(title, css, js, data) is the sole producer of the render command's HTML. It returns a template literal: `<!doctype html>`, `<html lang="en">`, charset meta, viewport meta, `<title>` (escaped), `<style>${css}</style>`, `<main id="root"></main>`, `<script type="application/json" id="page-data">`, `<script>${inlineScript(js)}</script>`, `</html>` plus a trailing newline. It emits no story-helper script tag, no <link>, no external src, and no <head>/<body> tags.

facts.claim: The order of elements in the page is: title, style, #root, data-block script, bundle script. The data block comes before the bundle. client.tsx throws if the #page-data element is absent when it runs, so the data script must stay before the bundle script. A helper script tag has no existing position and nothing in the code fixes where one would go.

facts.claim: escapeHtml, the only HTML escaper in render.ts, escapes only `&` and `<` (not `>` and not quotes). It is a module-private const and is used only for the title. It is therefore NOT safe for an attribute value, and render.ts has no attribute-escaper. An escaper for data-declaration / data-member values would be a new capability or would have to live in app.tsx, which the area does not cover. app.tsx is the scope of another explorer.
facts.evidence: render.ts:38 `const escapeHtml = (s) => s.replace(/&/g,'&').replace(/</g,'<')`; render.ts:65 sole call site. render.test.ts:54-60 asserts `</title><script>bad()</script>` becomes `</title><script>bad()</script>`.

facts.claim: The render command writes to disk exactly once: a single writeFileSync(out, pageHtml(...)) at render.ts:174-182. Everything before it is reads and console output. Order inside renderWith: (1) loaded(file) YAML parse, returning notDrawn (exit 1, no file) on a parse failure; (2) if the doc is a highlight, resolve the target, print wrong-highlight lines and a '<n> marked' line; (3) rulebookFor, printing faults to stderr; (4) checkedAgainst, printing '<n> found, and drawn on the page' to stdout; (5) await bundle(); (6) read style.css and syntax.css, joined with '\n'; (7) writeFileSync; (8) console.log '<out> — <KB>KB, drawn in the browser by React', returns 0. No file other than `out` is written.

facts.claim: The page's bytes are a pure string template over four inputs: title, css, js bundle text, and one JSON data block. pageHtml has no timestamp, random value, hash, counter, version string or path in it.
facts.evidence: ts/metalang/render.ts:58-69 (pageHtml returns a fixed template with title, css, DATA_ID block, inlineScript(js)). grep for Date|Math.random|performance|crypto|randomUUID|process.env|cwd over every non-test ts/metalang source returns only import.meta.url/here (path resolution) and import.meta.main entry guards; no clock or randomness.

facts.claim: Rendering one document twice already produces identical bytes, in the repo path and in the kit path, and the two paths produce the same bytes as each other. Probe: render ts/metalang/arch.yaml twice via `bun run ts/metalang/render.ts` gave sha256 4b63175167d67926c49f389a85348429d669866a94a7e73bdee262205f98ca04 both times; two runs of `node k1/kit.js render` on the same file gave the same hash; the kit and repo renders compare equal (cmp).
facts.evidence: Command output pasted from this run (bun 1.2.14, arch.yaml, 293KB): o1.html == o2.html == n1.html == n2.html == p1.html == p2.html, all 4b631751...ca04. Rendering from a different path of the same content (copy of arch.yaml elsewhere) also gave identical bytes (`pathindep`).

facts.claim: Two separate kit builds from the same tree and the same version string produce byte-identical files: kit.js, page.js, style.css, syntax.css, the three yaml files, package.json, README.md (diff of per-file sha256 printed KITSAME). page.js sha256 4c772e77c1712a1e7087eb38a28a0dd05813451cc185e0e6cd43204fb4b4f80d and kit.js cfc0dcf4137dbd51a1a41d1766e816d1402106e221cbd87ff2215f1dfccb4a98 in both builds. Bundles contain no absolute paths (grep for the home dir and scratchpad path counted 0 in kit.js, page.js, and the rendered page).
facts.evidence: `bun run ts/metalang/kit.ts <dir> T` twice, `shasum -a 256 *` per dir, diff empty. Bundler is Bun.build with minify:true, sourcemap:'none', no define, target browser (ts/metalang/bundle.ts bundlePage, SHARED config); page bundle is built by bundlePage(join(here, PAGE_SOURCE), {}) at kit.ts:~140 and by builtPageBundle at render.ts:~187.

facts.claim: The kit version string reaches only package.json and README.md, never kit.js, page.js, or a rendered page, so changing the version changes those two files and nothing a page is made from. Probe: build with version OTHER vs T differed only in package.json and README.md.
facts.evidence: kit.ts writes version via JSON.stringify({name,version,...}) and readmeText(version) only; diff of k3 vs k1 sums showed only package.json and README.md lines changed. The CI step passes the release tag as that version: .github/workflows/ci.yml:592 `bun run ts/metalang/kit.ts dist/evolang-kit "$TAG"`.

facts.claim: The only things in the page that could vary are object/Map key order and array order in the JSON data block, and all of them come from deterministic sources: JSON.stringify(data) follows insertion order, which comes from yaml.load of the file, the rulebook's declared words (Map/Object built in document order), the checker's problem list, and `[...marks.marked]` which is a Map built in highlight-entry order. No Set or Map is iterated in an order set by hashes, time or the filesystem in the render path; the one sort found is words.ts:604 with a total tiebreak `y.deep - x.deep || x.at - y.at`.
facts.evidence: render.ts:176-186 builds the data object; page-data.ts:marksFrom/PageMarks and dataBlock = JSON.stringify(data).replace(/</g,'\\u003c') (page-data.ts:~57); highlight.ts:220 `new Map<string,string>()` built in entry order; words.ts:604 sort. Inference, not proven for every document: order stability rests on insertion order being stable, which was only probed on arch.yaml, not on a highlight file or a document that fails the check.

facts.claim: No existing test asserts byte stability of a rendered page or of a kit. The tests that touch pageHtml/renderWith assert containment (title escaped, `</script` neutralised, data block escaped, renderWith writes a file), never that two renders are equal.
facts.evidence: grep -n -i 'byte|identical|determin|twice|same bytes|digest|sha' over render.test.ts, kit.test.ts, bundle.test.ts, page-data.test.ts, cli.test.ts returns nothing relevant (only unrelated 'shared'). pageHtml tests: render.test.ts:45,55,63,95,259,267; renderWith tests: render.test.ts:277,290. kit.test.ts:140-166 draws a page under node and checks the document is in the page and that page.js is carried, with no repeat-render comparison.

facts.claim: Nothing named `installation.json` exists in this working tree, and there is no digest file for the kit. The issue and brief mention the kit's own `installation.json` digests, but a repo-wide grep finds no file or reference. The only kit release machinery is the CI zip step, which writes no digest.
facts.evidence: grep -rIl 'installation.json' (excluding node_modules/.git) returned empty; `git ls-files | grep -i installation` returned empty. ci.yml:577-599 builds dist/evolang-kit, checks required files non-empty, and runs `zip -r evolang-kit.zip evolang-kit`; no sha256 step in that block. The word `digest` in the issue's completion evidence ('kit release digest') therefore refers to something outside this tree (JARVIS side) or something not yet written.

facts.claim: What would break byte stability for a pinned kit is the toolchain, not the page code: the bundle text depends on Bun's bundler/minifier version and on react/react-dom/js-yaml versions. Both are pinned: .bun-version is 1.2.14 and package.json pins react 19.3.0, react-dom 19.3.0, js-yaml 4.1.0; CI installs with `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and reads bun-version-file .bun-version.
facts.evidence: .bun-version content `1.2.14`; package.json dependencies; ci.yml:434 and :580 `bun-version-file: .bun-version`; ci.yml:591 `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. Local probe ran under bun 1.2.14, same as the pin.

facts.claim: Adding data-declaration / data-member attributes and the story script tag changes the bytes of page.js (the bundle) and of pageHtml's template, so every previously rendered page and every kit digest changes once; after that, byte stability depends only on the new code not introducing a non-deterministic id source. Any member identity derived by walking a shape's properties must follow document order (Object.keys on yaml-loaded mappings), not a Set or sort without a total tiebreak.
facts.evidence: Inference from render.ts:58-69 (shell is the template) and the build path in kit.ts/bundle.ts; app.tsx draws `section.d-decl` and member `tr` rows in the Table; app.tsx uses Object.entries/Object.keys/new Map/new Set at lines 128, 342, 466, 961, 1021, 1112, 1353, 1723 (all insertion-ordered). Not yet built, so this is a forecast, not a measured fact.

facts.claim: Escaping in the shell is narrow: escapeHtml escapes only `&` and `<` and is used for the title only. Attribute values written by React (the new data-declaration / data-member) are escaped by React's DOM, not by pageHtml, so the escaping requirement for ids with quotes lives in the bundle, and the server-side shell escape does not cover attribute context.
facts.evidence: render.ts:36 `const escapeHtml = (s) => s.replace(/&/g,'&').replace(/</g,'<')`; used only at render.ts:63 in <title>. A new `<script src="/api/packages/story.js">` tag would be a constant string in the template, adding no variable input.
